title: Ekström wins a four-safety-car Zandvoort thriller
dek: Mattias Ekström won at Zandvoort from eighth on the grid, 7.414 seconds clear of champion Marco Wittmann, as four safety cars wrecked pole-sitter Mike Rockenfeller's strategy and gave Audi its first win of 2014.

chapters.title: A champion in the dunes
text: Marco Wittmann arrived at Zandvoort already crowned. The BMW Team RMG driver had clinched the drivers' title at the Lausitzring two weeks earlier, finishing sixth in the eighth round of ten to leave himself on 128 points, 69 clear of Christian Vietoris with two races to go. Pascal Wehrlein had won that race for Mercedes, while Wittmann, with four victories, could now race for pride and for the team and manufacturer tables.

The fight behind him was wide open. Vietoris led the chase on 59 points, Mattias Ekström and Edoardo Mortara were level on 56 and Mike Rockenfeller had 54. Audi, meanwhile, had gone through eight races without a win.

The Circuit Park Zandvoort race, the ninth of the ten, ran with a mandatory pit stop, soft option and harder prime tyres and DRS for overtaking, a combination that suited a short, narrow circuit with little run-off. Twenty-three cars took part, from Audi, BMW and Mercedes. On a track with little run-off and few places to overtake, the timing of the compulsory stop looked likely to matter as much as raw speed.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller takes pole by 0.026 seconds
text: Qualifying ran in three knockout stages. Jamie Green was fastest in Q1 with 1:30.610, which cost António Félix da Costa, Augusto Farfus, Robert Wickens, Daniel Juncadella and Vitaly Petrov their places, while Q2 became a four-way scramble in the final minutes, with Nico Müller, Mortara, Green and Wehrlein each taking turns at the top before Wehrlein's 1:30.449 settled it. Ten drivers, among them Vietoris, Timo Scheider and Gary Paffett, went out there.

Rockenfeller then took pole with a gamble. He used his first set of tyres for only an out-lap and went straight back to the garage, saving them for a second set on which he set 1:30.713. Wittmann, Mortara and Ekström each made a single run; Wittmann was second, 0.026 seconds slower, and Mortara was third on 1:30.757.

The grid then changed. Mortara was sent to the back of the grid for a breach of the rules, while Ekström, who had been fourth, was moved back five places for blocking Paffett and started eighth. That promoted Green to third, with Müller, Wehrlein and Tomczyk behind and Joey Hand seventh. Wehrlein was the best of the Mercedes drivers in fifth, and Vietoris started 17th.

chapters.title: Wittmann leads, then Rockenfeller passes him
text: Wittmann out-accelerated Rockenfeller on the run to the first corner and took the lead, with Tomczyk also getting past Green. Behind the leaders Müller, from fourth on the grid, had made a strong start and was running third.

The first safety car came in the opening laps. Adrien Tambay ran onto the grass at the fast Turn 9 while pushing Paffett and lost the Audi into the barrier, which ended his race after four laps. The restart brought no changes at the front, and Wittmann pulled away again, but his soft tyres soon faded. Rockenfeller closed up, Wittmann braked late at Turn 1, and on lap 16 the Audi driver went through on the inside. Wittmann pitted for hard tyres at once, as did Tomczyk, and that early stop was to prove worth a great deal.

chapters.title: The wrong moment for the leaders
text: The second safety car arrived when Juncadella ran into the back of Farfus at the slow chicane and sent the BMW into the barriers. Rockenfeller led from Müller, Green, Scheider, da Costa and Ekström, but the cars at the front were all still on soft tyres and still had to stop, so the neutralisation cancelled their lead and left Wittmann, who had already made his stop, in a far better position.

When racing resumed the stops came in a rush. Ekström and Vietoris were among those who changed tyres and Wittmann, driving through traffic, moved back up to third. Then Müller, running second at one point, was touched by Vietoris and went into the wall, which brought out the third safety car. Rockenfeller stayed out on soft tyres and was the only leading car yet to stop, so his race was effectively over.

chapters.title: Ekström storms through on option tyres
text: Ekström was only ninth at the restart, but as the best-placed driver on options he had both fresher tyres and time to use them. He passed Hand and Wehrlein in quick succession, caught Tomczyk and went by Wittmann for the lead, while Rockenfeller finally stopped and rejoined down the order, eventually finishing 15th.

A fourth safety car followed when Paffett ran onto the grass in the same way as Tambay and lost control, but the restart changed nothing at the front. Ekström won by 7.414 seconds from Wittmann, who also set the fastest lap, with Tomczyk third, 11.144 seconds behind. Mortara, who had started last, was fourth after fending off Vietoris, who had come through from 17th on soft tyres to take fifth. Maxime Martin held sixth ahead of Wehrlein, with Wickens eighth and Scheider and Hand rounding out the top ten. Bruno Spengler spun Green late in the race and was penalised for it.

chapters.title: Audi break their duck, BMW take the team title
text: Ekström called the safety cars helpful and the victory special, saying the car had been quick, and Audi's DTM head Dieter Gass said the team had finally got its first win of the season. Mortara said it had been hard to stay motivated on race morning after the penalty, yet the team's strategy and a superb pit stop took him from last to fourth. Gass praised that recovery, but he was critical of the stewards for taking no action over the Vietoris and Müller incident.

Rockenfeller, the pole-sitter who led much of the race, finished 15th and said his race had been spoiled by the safety car and the regulations, while Phoenix team director Ernst Moser called his the fastest car in the field and the result a bitter pill. Müller was out after the contact with Vietoris, and Green lost points when Spengler spun him. Juncadella, whose contact had sent Farfus into the barriers, was given a 30-second penalty after the race that dropped him from eighth on the road to 17th, while Spengler, penalised for the incident with Green, was classified 16th.

For BMW the day was a good one, even without the win: motorsport director Jens Marquardt said the many safety cars had forced constant strategy changes and turned the closing laps into a sprint. Wittmann was second, and the result was enough to give BMW Team RMG the team championship with a race to spare, a second championship for the squad within a fortnight. Wittmann said Ekström was simply faster on options and that the early stop had been the right call, and he set his sights on winning the finale at Hockenheim. Tomczyk's third place gave BMW a second car on the podium.

In the standings Wittmann went to 146 points, with Ekström up to second on 81, ahead of Vietoris on 69, Mortara on 68, Rockenfeller on 54 and Martin on 47. That left second place in the championship as the main prize for the finale, on 19 October at the Hockenheimring, where BMW also had the manufacturers' title to fight for.

facts.v: The race was interrupted four times, by Tambay, by Farfus after Juncadella's contact, by Müller after contact with Vietoris, and by Paffett.

facts.v: Ekström ended a drought of more than 1,000 days, his first DTM win since Valencia 2011, and gave Audi its first victory of the season.
